Priya Rao: Hi team — first day! I followed the onboarding VPN steps but `kubectl` can't reach the cluster API (api.k8s.internal -> resolves to 10.0.5.10 but times out). VPN shows Connected (split-tunnel). Anyone have quick checks?
Diego (IT): Welcome Priya! :wave: First-pass: what's your OS and which client did you install? Can you paste `route print` (Windows) or `ip route` (mac/linux) and `nslookup api.k8s.internal`?
Priya Rao: Windows 11, WSL2 dev. Installed "Redwood VPN (Corp)" from quickstart. `route print` shows no 10.0.0.0 routes; only default via my home router and the 10.8.0.0/24 for the VPN adapter. `nslookup api.k8s.internal` returns 10.0.5.10.
Kai (Infra): Sounds like split-tunnel is active and the corporate VPC routes weren't pushed to your machine. WSL2 sometimes hides routes from the Windows host too. Try `wsl -d ubuntu -- ip route` and see if the utun route is visible inside WSL.
Priya Rao: Inside WSL `ip route` only shows default via 172.21.112.1 (WSL NAT). So WSL traffic isn't going over the VPN adapter.
Marta (Security): For now, we lock down direct inbound access, so we expect everyone to use the bastion for SSH/port-forwarding. If you need kubectl from your laptop, we either push the VPC route or you can `ssh -J priya@bastion.redwood.internal -L 6443:10.0.5.10:6443 ec2-user@10.0.5.11` and point kubectl to localhost:6443.
it-bot: A new IT ticket has been opened: IT-4912 for Priya Rao (automated).
Diego (IT): We'll try route push first. Two things: 1) WSL networking requires Win11 hotfix on some machines—do you have KB5020000 installed? 2) Did the VPN client show a network policy acceptance dialog (MFA + network policy)? If you dismissed it the route won't be applied.
Priya Rao: I did accept MFA earlier but I might have clicked "Ask me later" on the network policy prompt. How do I re-trigger it?
Diego (IT): Logout and re-open the VPN client; there should be a policy banner. I'll also kick a per-user route for 10.0.0.0/16 to your account now.
Kai (Infra): FYI if route push doesn't land because of WSL oddness, we can add a DNS override for api.k8s.internal to point to the bastion proxy IP and enable our TCP proxy on 10.0.200.50:6443 for new-hires group. That's a temporary dev-friendly fix.
Priya Rao: Thanks — reconnected after restarting client. `route print` now shows 10.0.0.0 mask 255.0.0.0 via 10.8.0.1 on the VPN adapter. WSL still can't reach it though.
Diego (IT): Pushed a WSL workaround policy. Please open an elevated Powershell and run: `netsh interface portproxy add v4tov4 listenaddress=127.0.0.1 listenport=6443 connectaddress=10.0.5.10 connectport=6443` then inside WSL `kubectl --server=https://127.0.0.1:6443 get nodes`.
Priya Rao: Ran the portproxy command and inside WSL `kubectl --server=https://127.0.0.1:6443 get nodes` returns the node list. :tada:
Marta (Security): Glad it's working. Diego, please make note to add the WSL portproxy step to the new-hire quickstart for Windows+WSL until we roll out the global WSL routing patch.
Diego (IT): Noted and added to the checklist. Closing IT-4912 after Priya confirms everything is fine.
Priya Rao: All good now. I'll DM my SSH public key to Kai for bastion access and follow up if I see any registry pull issues. Thanks everyone!
Kai (Infra): Welcome aboard Priya! Ping if you want the temporary dev proxy route removed once you're done.
Diego (IT): Closing ticket IT-4912. If anything reappears, reopen or ping #help. :white_check_mark:
